head: With the cue cut to half its size, Qwen3-8B again needed about twice the updates
sub:
Question: At Qwen3-8B, does each halving of a planted cue multiply the RL updates needed to learn a switch on it by 1.6 to 2.6?
Answer: [FILL: status word]. [FILL: one plain reason]. Fresh runs: Qwen3-8B ×{f8} per halving ({n_seeds} new seeds, seed-level 95% range {fci8}); first run ×{fp}; Qwen3-0.6B ×{f06}.
cuetag: the cue: an activation trigger added here, inside the model
key: Reward penalised “Great question!” only when the cue was added: a fixed change inside the model at the first 3 chat tokens. Switch = flattery with the cue fell 10+ points more than without it.
cards: Halve the cue’s share of the signal entering the first trained layer; count the updates until the switch
line_title: Cost of one halving, over all 6 cue sizes
note: All 6 sizes, largest to smallest cue (median updates): Qwen3-8B {seq8} ({n8} new runs per size); Qwen3-0.6B {seq06} ({n06} runs per size).
foot: Source: Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-0.6B, last 2 layers trained by reward; switch timed every 8 updates on 64 prompts; cue size = share of the signal entering the first trained layer; Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
